issue.title: middleware, agent plugins: an edit to a file the module imports isn't loaded until its entry file changes
issue.body:
Came up while going through the size-and-time caches next to the gateway after #3708. A JS gateway plugin's module can import files beside it (`jsmod.Compile` reads them), but `stamp()` in internal/middleware/middleware.go only has plugins.json, plugins/package.json and bun.lock, and each middleware's entry file. So when only a file the entry imports changes, the middleware is never loaded again: the old code keeps running until the entry or plugins.json changes, or magpie restarts. A fix to an import that didn't compile is missed the same way, so the Plugins page keeps showing the old load error.

The docs say it should be picked up: "magpie looks at the files and plugins.json once a second, and loads a middleware again when they changed" (site/public/docs/plugins.html), and the Reload line in docs/subsystems/gateway-middleware.md.

On 7a60e78c: a folder plugin whose index.js imports a model map from ./names.js. After names.js is rewritten (another size, a later time), requests still get the old mapping. internal/agentplug's `stamp()` has the same shape: an agent module whose `name` comes from ./name.js still has the old name after name.js is edited.

It only bites someone working on a plugin of their own added from a folder. A package from npm or git is replaced whole on update, and that changes bun.lock, which is stamped.

I'll take it. The plan: `jsmod.Compile` also gives back the files it imported, each with its time and size from just before it was read, and both loaders load again when one of them changed.

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/3723-import-stamps` (head `e232a777`, on upstream `6afbe3f3`) — a middleware or agent plugin reloads when a module it imports changes.

**Root cause.** `internal/middleware/middleware.go`'s `stamp()` folds `plugin.ListStamp()` and each middleware's own file mtime/size; `internal/agentplug/agentplug.go` has the same stamp; `jsmod.Compile` returned only the module, so what a module imported was invisible to both.

**Change.** `jsmod.Compile` also reports the files it read (path, mtime nanos, size, taken just before each read); both stamps fold those paths' current stat, and a loaded set re-stamps itself after loading — without that the first look reloads forever (`TestRequestChain` caught it).

**Verified.** Red: `go test -tags nogui ./internal/middleware/ ./internal/agentplug/ -run TestReloadOnImportedChange` → `middleware: reload_imports_test.go:41: an imported change didn't reload: {"model":"m1","v":"one"}` and `agentplug: reload_imports_test.go:59: an imported change didn't reload`
Green: `both → PASS; `./internal/middleware` 31 tests, `./internal/agentplug` and `./internal/jsmod` ok; `-race -count=2` green` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/middleware` + `agentplug`

Not covered: a file added to the graph by a dynamic `import()` — only static imports are read.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 26's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6afbe3f3` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3723-import-stamps — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.
